name: stri_isempty
title: Determine if a String is of Length Zero

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

origin.details: An empty string is true. Any other string, including one that contains only combining marks, is false. A missing string stays missing.
origin.value: A logical vector the same length as str.
origin.example:
x <- stri_isempty(c("", NA, "a"))
cat(paste0("stri_isempty(c(\"\", NA, \"a\")) returns ", paste(ifelse(is.na(x), "NA", ifelse(x, "TRUE", "FALSE")), collapse = ", "), ".\n"))

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, a number, a complex value, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

translation.details: An empty string is true. The string "NA" is false. A missing character is NA, not false. Coercion matches stri_length, so a number is empty only when its character form is empty.
translation.value: True, False, or NA. A list or tuple returns a list. None returns an empty list.
translation.example:
from stringi.length import stri_isempty
from stringi._na import NA
x = stri_isempty(["", NA, "a"])
shown = ", ".join("NA" if value is NA else ("TRUE" if value else "FALSE") for value in x)
print(f"stri_isempty([\"\", NA, \"a\"]) returns {shown}.")
